summary: Hosted by Barr Yaron (Partner at Amplify Partners) at the AI Engineer Summit 2025 in New York, Frontier Feud adapts the Family Feud format for AI engineers. Two teams compete by guessing the most popular survey answers from 100 AI engineers. Team 'Roo's basilisk' includes Mahir/M and John (Anthropic), Tina (Reflection AI), and Sha (Google Gemini developer APIs). Team 'Paige attention' includes Paige (Google DeepMind), Colin (Augment Code, formerly Meta FAIR), Petra (Google factuality PM), and Stephen (joining Thinking Machines). During introductions, participants shared tech hot takes: M predicted one of roughly five organizations training big models will stop by year's end; John believes AIs make good therapists; Tina recommended 20 minutes daily of non-AI thinking with paper and pencil; Sha echoed Tina, noting future AI agents will need good human content to train on; Paige predicted most deployed models will be on-device within 18 months using smaller specialized models orchestrated together; Colin argued Transformers aren't the final architecture since models will eventually use biological materials, and dating apps will become AIs dating each other; Petra claimed one-on-one bot conversations are boring and future chats will include multiple bots; Stephen dismissed token wall concerns as a skill issue. Three rounds were played. Round 1 asked for the most influential AI researcher with Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Hinton, Yann LeCun, Andrew Ng, Fei-Fei Li, and Yoshua Bengio on the board. Round 2 asked for top considerations when choosing a model with cost as the number one answer, followed by latency, accuracy, capabilities, and CEO; the steal answer 'open source vs closed source' earned Paige attention 63 points. Round 3 asked for tired AI buzzwords with AGI as number one, plus agents, RAG, and prompt engineering. Roo's basilisk won overall and advanced to fast money, where Mahir answered four of five questions, accumulating 140 points with Cursor (favorite AI tool, number one answer), software engineers (most at-risk job, number three), 'Attention is All You Need' (most influential paper, number one), and hardware failure (2am nightmare, accepted). John then took the second turn, answering model APIs (AI tool, third answer), artists/content creation (at-risk job, ambiguous), 'Attention is All You Need' (already taken by Mahir), a VC cold email and CUDA issues (2am nightmare), and Healthcare (industry benefiting most from AI, number one answer). The team did not reach 200 points, losing the fast money bonus but remaining overall winners. The number one answers revealed were Cursor, data entry, 'Attention is All You Need,' model outage, and Healthcare. Prizes included a massive llama plushie, rainbow llama beanie babies, AI engineering books, and NYC restaurant gift cards. Barr announced a comprehensive state-of-AI-engineering survey to be presented at the June AI Engineer World's Fair.

sections.title: Introduction and Team Hot Takes
sections.summary: Barr Yaron introduces Frontier Feud, explains the Family Feud format using a survey of 100 AI engineers, and has participants introduce themselves with tech hot takes. Participants include M and John (Anthropic), Tina (Reflection AI), Sha (Google Gemini APIs), Paige (Google DeepMind), Colin (Augment Code/ex-FAIR), Petra (Google factuality), and Stephen (Thinking Machines). Hot takes cover predictions about model training consolidation, AI therapists, non-AI thinking time, on-device models, biological computing architectures, multi-bot conversations, and token walls.

sections.title: Round 1: Most Influential AI Researcher
sections.summary: Mahir and Paige face off. Mahir guesses Ilya Sutskever (not on board) and his team plays. Correct guesses include Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Hinton, and Yann LeCun. Incorrect guesses include Sam Altman and another name, producing strikes. The opposing team attempts to steal with Jeff Dean but fails, so Roo's basilisk keeps the points. Other board answers include Andrew Ng, Fei-Fei Li, and Yoshua Bengio.

sections.title: Round 2: Top Considerations When Choosing a Model
sections.summary: John and Colin face off. Colin guesses intelligence (on board). Tina guesses cost (number one answer). Additional correct answers include latency, accuracy/performance, and CEO. Safety and on-prem serving are not on the board. Paige attention steals with 'open source vs closed source' for 63 points.

sections.title: Round 3: AI Buzzword Everyone Is Tired Of
sections.summary: Petra and Tina face off. Tina guesses agents (on board). Sha guesses multimodality (not on board), co-pilots (not on board). AGI is the number one answer. Deep seek and safety are not on the board. Additional answers include RAG and prompt engineering. Roo's basilisk wins the round and the game overall.

sections.title: Fast Money Round and Conclusion
sections.summary: Mahir answers fast money questions first, accumulating 140 points across four answers: Cursor (favorite AI tool, number one), software engineers (most at-risk job, number three), 'Attention is All You Need' (most influential paper, number one), and hardware failure (2am nightmare, accepted). John takes the second turn with 25 seconds for five questions, answering model APIs (AI tool, third answer), artists mapped to content creation/writing (at-risk job, ambiguous), 'Attention is All You Need' (already taken by Mahir), VC cold email and CUDA issues (2am nightmare), and Healthcare (industry benefiting most, number one). The team did not reach 200 points, losing the fast money bonus but remaining overall winners. Barr reveals all number one answers: Cursor, data entry, 'Attention is All You Need,' model outage, and Healthcare. Prizes include a massive llama plushie, rainbow llama beanie babies, AI engineering books, and NYC restaurant gift cards. Barr announces a comprehensive state-of-AI-engineering survey to be presented at the June AI Engineer World's Fair.
